title: Input encoding, hidden features and a tied text head
description: Terms for the vector boundary, its causal layout and the shared table used by text lookup and vocabulary projection.

terms.definition: A source-to-vector adapter that supplies checked embedding sequences to the causal backbone. The implemented text encoder reuses token lookup; this adapter is not the bidirectional encoder stack of an encoder-decoder Transformer.

The embedding tensor, sequence layout, graph-recording context and live bindings checked before the backbone consumes vectors. Token IDs, vocabulary, targets and text loss masks stay outside this generic carrier.

The batch and position shape, active prefix length of each row, causal range start for each cell and explicit RoPE positions. These values describe where attention may read and which positions RoPE uses.
A borrowing view of the existing decoder blocks and final RMSNorm. It transforms residual-width input vectors into residual-width hidden features without requiring a text vocabulary or output table.
The vocabulary projection that multiplies hidden features by the transpose of the live text embedding table. Its output has one logit per text vocabulary entry at each supplied position.
Using one learned table for both token lookup and the text output projection. The allocation is counted once, and backward adds lookup-path and head-path contributions to its gradient.

The exact parameter nodes and value revisions captured when vectors are prepared and checked again when the backbone consumes them. A descriptive source label cannot authorize stale vectors after a learned producer or backbone parameter changes.
